# Mechanical Back Strain

**Authors:** David Yusupov, Todd May

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Back pain is one of the most frequent chief complaints in the emergency department and a leading cause of disability and healthcare expenditures worldwide, affecting individuals across all ages and backgrounds. Mechanical back strain is a specific subtype of back pain resulting from injury or overuse of the spinal muscles, ligaments, tendons, intervertebral discs, or surrounding soft tissues. The anatomy of the lumbar spine, including vertebrae, intervertebral discs, facet joints, and supporting musculature, plays a critical role in both the development and resolution of mechanical strain. Most mechanical back strains follow a benign natural history, with symptoms resolving over days to weeks with conservative management; however, pain may occasionally radiate along predictable patterns, reflecting the involvement of paraspinal muscles and neural structures. Healthcare clinicians must remain vigilant for red flags indicating more emergent or serious etiologies, as delayed diagnosis can lead to high morbidity and mortality.[1]
